  "description": "Expanded Series Bible III #09 We Bought It Together reusable adult idea-source engine. Generates premises in which {{char}} and {{user}} jointly acquire a significant shared asset that forces an ongoing practical partnership, varying the asset, the money, the work and every interpersonal outcome.",
  "source_version": "1.0",
  "bible": {
    "document": "Character Card Forge — Series Bible III",
    "version": "0.4",
    "entry": "9",
    "kind": "series"
  },
  "summary": "Adult {{char}} and {{user}} jointly acquire something significant that creates an ongoing practical relationship: a small business, fixer-upper, campervan, boat, workshop, expensive hobby machine, holiday property, vehicle, arcade cabinet, studio equipment or other shared asset. The engine is the recurring contact the shared ownership forces: money, maintenance, scheduling, decisions and disagreements that keep bringing the two back to the same table. Ownership creates obligation and familiarity, never a script for romance, conflict or success.",
  "core_premise": "{{char}} and {{user}} own something together. The asset is significant enough that neither can walk away casually, and practical reality — costs, repairs, permits, bookings, operating hours — forces them into recurring contact and shared decisions. The premise fixes only the joint ownership and what the asset is; who wanted it more, who pays, who works, who benefits, whether it thrives or collapses, and what the two become to each other are all open. Shared ownership establishes no cohabitation, no shared finances beyond the asset and no romance by default.",
  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult roleplay opening around a shared asset. Establish what {{char}} and {{user}} bought, roughly how the ownership and money are split, why they bought it together, and the immediate practical situation that forces their next shared decision — a breakdown, a bill, a booking, a deadline, a season opening or a quiet month. Give {{char}} a defined life, skills, history with the asset and reasons for wanting it. Open at a playable moment where the partnership's texture shows: a working bee, a handover, a settlement day or a hard conversation about the numbers. Do not script {{user}}'s feelings, effort, attraction or choices, and leave the partnership's future unwritten.",
  "core_variables": [
    "What the shared asset is: small business, fixer-upper, campervan, boat, workshop, hobby machine, holiday property, vehicle, arcade cabinet, studio equipment or another significant purchase.",
    "Why {{char}} and {{user}} bought it together: affordability, romance, friendship, circumstance, persuasion, investment or impulse.",
    "The ownership split and how formal it is: equal shares, unequal shares, handshake or contract.",
    "Cost, debt and financial pressure: what the asset earns versus what it drains each month.",
    "Whether one person pushed the idea, and how the other's agreement was reached.",
    "Repair, maintenance and operating requirements, and who can actually meet them.",
    "Scheduling conflicts and competing demands on each owner's time.",
    "Whether the asset is profitable, useful, ridiculous, or all three at once.",
    "What each owner contributed: money, labour, skills, contacts or presence.",
    "The history between {{char}} and {{user}} before the purchase: strangers, friends, exes, colleagues, family.",
    "External pressures: landlords, inspectors, competitors, customers, family opinions.",
    "The first real test the opening places on the partnership.",
    "How honest each owner has been about money, effort and intent.",
    "Whether either owner wants out, and whether the other knows.",
    "{{char}}'s life and identity beyond the asset: work, home, friends, other commitments.",
    "Whether the partnership ends, changes, or endures — deliberately left open."

  "generation_rules": [
    "Do not write {{user}} for the player or define {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue, consent, effort levels, financial contributions or future behaviour unless the source explicitly supplies that fact.",
    "Character belief is not objective truth; keep {{char}}'s assumptions about {{user}}'s reliability, wealth, motives or commitment distinct from verified facts.",
    "Do not pre-play outcomes. Leave cooperation, conflict, honesty, exit, sale, romance and the asset's fate open.",
    "All characters are adults.",
    "Shared ownership of an asset does not create romantic or sexual consent, cohabitation or merged finances.",
    "Cohabitation, travel together, one bed at the asset, physical closeness during repairs and financial entanglement do not create blanket consent.",
    "Sex or intimacy, if it ever develops, must not erase a character's baseline personality, goals, nonsexual interests, judgement or boundaries.",
    "Do not force romance into the partnership. Practical cooperation, friendship, rivalry, unresolved tension, businesslike distance or no relationship change are all valid outcomes.",
    "Shared ownership establishes the asset and its decisions only: not a household, not joint bank accounts, not a relationship label.",
    "Make practical decisions — money, repairs, schedules, bookings — part of the roleplay engine rather than background noise the story skips.",
    "Vary what the asset is across generations; do not default every card to the same business or vehicle type.",
    "Vary the ownership split and how formal or informal it is; a handshake partnership behaves differently from a contracted one.",
    "Let {{char}} keep a full life beyond the asset: occupation where relevant, friends, family, interests and boundaries that are not the shared purchase.",
    "Financial pressure, breakdowns and deadlines create urgency, never mandated fights, confessions or reconciliations.",
    "Third parties — landlords, inspectors, competitors, relatives, customers — may pressure the partnership, but do not use them to railroad {{user}}'s choices.",
    "An owner wanting to sell, buy out or exit is a proposal or a secret, never a settled outcome that overrides {{user}}'s agency.",
    "Vary skill, competence and effort independently; neither owner is automatically the competent one or the lazy one.",
    "Do not treat the asset's commercial failure or success as a moral verdict on either owner.",
    "Keep any intimacy non-graphic and grounded in the partnership's practical texture: shared work, money and time.",
    "Preserve {{user}}'s right to renegotiate terms, refuse tasks, set boundaries, or exit the partnership at any point in play.",
    "Overlap boundary: distinct from Our Little Business, which centres on running the venture; here the joint acquisition and its ongoing obligations are the engine. Distinct from Temporary Partners, where the partnership has a defined end.",
    "Open at a playable moment where the partnership's stakes are visible without having resolved them."

  "guardrails": [
    "All participants are adults.",
    "No scripted {{user}} feelings, dialogue, effort, consent or future decisions.",
    "Shared ownership is practical entanglement, not automatic intimacy, obligation or romance.",
    "Consent is activity-specific; sharing an asset, a bed at the property or a working weekend never implies sexual consent.",
    "No predetermined reconciliation, breakup, buyout, bankruptcy or success for the partnership.",
    "Character beliefs about money, effort or each other are viewpoints, not narrator-endorsed facts.",
    "Financial pressure and shared debt must not be used to coerce intimacy or compliance from {{user}}.",
    "Third-party pressure does not override {{user}}'s agency or force a single resolution.",
    "Keep the asset's dangers and physical demands realistic without staging mandatory injuries.",
    "Keep any intimacy non-graphic and secondary to the partnership's practical decisions.",
    "Do not force romance, sex or conflict where the premise supports calm cooperation, friendship or businesslike distance.",
    "{{char}} remains a complete person beyond the shared asset: her own life, history, interests and boundaries.",
    "Every major partnership decision — sell, expand, dissolve, restructure — stays open for {{user}} to influence or make."

    {
      "id": "asset",
      "label": "What they bought",
      "content": "Vary the asset across the full range: small business, fixer-upper, campervan, boat, workshop, hobby machine, holiday property, project vehicle, arcade cabinet, studio equipment or stranger variants. The asset should be concrete, inspectable and demanding, not a vague symbol."
    },
    {
      "id": "motive",
      "label": "Why they bought together",
      "content": "Establish why the purchase needed two people: affordability, romance, friendship, circumstance, persuasion or impulse. Who wanted it more, and how the other's agreement was obtained, colours every later decision."
    },
    {
      "id": "money",
      "label": "Ownership, debt and pressure",
      "content": "Set the split and how formal it is, plus the asset's real economics. Unequal shares, hidden debt, family loans and money-pit trajectories give the partnership texture; they must never coerce intimacy or dictate an outcome."
    },
    {
      "id": "work",
      "label": "Work, repair and skill",
      "content": "Decide who can actually do the work and who shows up. Skill gaps, quiet resentment, secret repairs, botched jobs and dangerous equipment keep the maintenance schedule a source of story rather than a checklist."
    },
    {
      "id": "time",
      "label": "Schedules and logistics",
      "content": "Give the asset a rhythm: weekend rituals, handover meetings, booking calendars, seasonal deadlines, distance. The logistics of sharing time is where most co-owner friction and most co-owner intimacy actually live."
    },
    {
      "id": "relations",
      "label": "What ownership does to the relationship",
      "content": "Let the pair's history and temperature vary — friends, exes, rivals, strangers, newlyweds — and let the shared work push them closer, further apart or nowhere in particular. Do not force romance or conflict as the destination."
    },
    {
      "id": "pressure",
      "label": "External pressures and third parties",
      "content": "Landlords, inspectors, competitors, customers, relatives and would-be partners can all press on the two owners. Use them to raise stakes, never to railroad {{user}}'s decisions or resolve the story on his behalf."
    },
    {
      "id": "user",
      "label": "{{user}}'s stake stays open",

  "raw_prompt": "Generate a non-graphic adult character-card premise for We Bought It Together. Adult {{char}} and {{user}} jointly own something significant — a small business, fixer-upper, campervan, boat, workshop, hobby machine, holiday property or similar — and its money, repairs, permits and scheduling force them into recurring contact and shared decisions. Vary what the asset is, why they bought together, the ownership split and how formal it is, who contributes money versus labour versus skills, their prior history, external pressures and the first real test the opening applies. Shared ownership creates obligation and familiarity, never automatic cohabitation, merged finances or romance; friendship, rivalry, businesslike distance, unresolved tension or no change are all valid outcomes. Do not script {{user}}'s feelings, effort or choices, and leave sale, dissolution, success and every relationship change open. All characters are adults; consent, boundaries and {{user}}'s autonomy remain in force."
